Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

anniversary noun

classical

Traupman 271: fēstus diēs anniversārius
Cic. Verr. 2.4.107: fēstōs diēs anniversāriōs

diēs anniversārius

anniversary, a day that comes round every year

anniversārius is “returning every year” (Lewis & Short): yearly feasts and rites are fēstī diēs anniversāriī and sacra anniversāria in Cicero.

Other words

  • nātālis, nātālis m. — anniversary (of the founding of a city, a colony, a temple)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 4.1.4; Plin. NH 14.55: nātālī urbis (Lewis & Short)

    Properly a birthday; transferred to “any anniversary, a commemorative festival” (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • ibi mihi Tulliola mea fuit praestō nātālī suō ipsō diē, quī cāsū īdem nātālis erat et Brundisīnae colōniae et tuae vīcīnae Salūtis

    my little Tullia was there to meet me on her very birthday, which happened also to be the anniversary of the colony of Brundisium and of your neighbour, the temple of SalusCic. Att. 4.1.4

  • ubi ūsque ad hoc tempus Syrācūsānī fēstōs diēs anniversāriōs agunt celeberrimō virōrum mulierumque conventū

    where to this day the Syracusans keep a yearly festival, with great crowds of men and womenCic. Verr. 2.4.107

See also birthday, festival, celebrate.

SourcesLewis & Short: anniversarius · Lewis & Short: natalis
